facts.statement: Eurofluvioviridavis lived in the Middle Eocene at the Messel Pit in Germany.
facts.quote: Eurofluvioviridavis is a genus of extinct birds from the Middle Eocene Messel Pit, Germany.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil SMNK.PAL.3835 was discovered in the lower middle Eocene Messel Pit near Darmstadt, Germany.
facts.quote: The holotype of Eurofluvioviridavis, SMNK.PAL.3835, was found in the lower middle Eocene Messel Pit, near Darmstadt, Germany, in the MP 11 Mammal Paleogene zone.

facts.statement: The species name robustipes refers to the animal's strongly built feet.
facts.quote: The specific ephitet, robustipes, is from Latin robustus, meaning robust, and pes, meaning foot, in reference to strongly built feet.

facts.statement: Eurofluvioviridavis had a wide, flattened beak similar to that of tyrant flycatchers.
facts.quote: Eurofluvioviridavis had a wide, flattened beak, resembling that of tyrant flycatchers.

facts.statement: The ulna was longer than the humerus and possessed eight to thirteen quill knobs.
facts.quote: The ulna is longer than the humerus, with eight to thirteen quill knobs indicating a relatively low number of secondary feathers.

facts.statement: The tarsometatarsus and feet of Eurofluvioviridavis resemble those of the genera Avolatavis and Vastanavis.
facts.quote: The tarsometatarsus and feet of Eurofluvioviridavis resemble those of Avolatavis and Vastanavis.

facts.statement: The semi-zygodactyl foot arrangement and raptor-like claws suggest Eurofluvioviridavis could grasp with its feet.
facts.quote: The feet show a semi-zygodactyl arrangement, and the ungual phalanges are raptor-like, possibly indicating that Eurofluvioviridavis could grasp with the foot.

facts.statement: Eurofluvioviridavis is related to Avolatavis and Vastanavis within the family Vastanavidae.
facts.quote: It is related to Avolatavis and Vastanavis, other members of the family Vastanavidae.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses support placing Vastanavis, Avolatavis, and Eurofluvioviridavis in the family Vastanavidae.
facts.quote: Cladistic analyses support a relationship between the genera Vastanavis, Avolatavis, and Eurofluvioviridavis in the family Vastanavidae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether vastanavids are stem-group relatives of parrots or part of the stem group of Psittacopasseres.
facts.quote: Their position relative to modern birds is not clear; it is possible that the vastanavids are stem-group relatives of the parrots, or that they are part of the stem group of the Psittacopasseres.

facts.statement: It is possible that Avolatavis is a junior synonym of Eurofluvioviridavis, though this cannot yet be confirmed.
facts.quote: Avolatavis has not been differentiated from Eurofluvioviridavis, meaning it is possible that the former taxon is a junior synonym.

facts.statement: Eurofluvioviridavis lived between 48.07 and 41.03 million years ago during the Lutetian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Lutetian (48.07 to 41.03 million years ago)
